summary: The Scout Launcher fires the Little Scout (Surveyor Probe Mk. IV), a launchable camera created by Slate to safely explore hazardous environments. It has photography, distance, seismic, ghost-matter, and warp-recall capabilities and is essential for solving many quantum and navigation puzzles.

behavior: The Little Scout has forward and rear-facing cameras for taking black-and-white images.
The Little Scout has a distance indicator.
The Little Scout has a seismic stability indicator, used on Brittle Hollow and on the Stranger's dam.
The Little Scout has a hazard indicator.
The Little Scout has a warp core for recall to the player.
When launched from the spaceship, the Scout exits at 150 m/s.
The Little Scout does not launch straight at the cross-hairs while piloting the ship; it launches slightly above and to the right.
lore: The Scout Launcher was created by Slate to help safely explore hazardous environments.
The Little Scout's formal name is the Surveyor Probe Mk. IV.
mechanics: The Scout can be launched from the spacesuit or from the ship.
On Xbox gamepad, the Scout is launched with the right bumper; on default PC keyboard and mouse, it is launched with the right mouse button.
Photographing the Quantum Moon with the Scout locks the Moon into its current position even when the player looks away.
Photographing the Nomai Statue in the Observatory with the Scout works the same way as on other quantum objects.
The Little Scout can be used to distract Anglerfish in Dark Bramble.
The Little Scout's cameras can detect Ghost Matter, which appears as a blue-green aura in photos.
The Little Scout can check the seismic stability of Brittle Hollow's crust and the Stranger's dam.
If the Scout is launched while on the Eye of the Universe, the player loses contact with it and cannot recall it.
The lost Eye-of-the-Universe Scout flies across the screen in the background during the post-credit scene.
Firing the Scout while jumping or in space causes a small recoil thrust that pushes the player away.
